_purpose: Stops that were PROPOSED FOR A TOUR and turned out to be outside the requested area. Which town a building stands in is a fact about geography, not an opinion — but PHASE 5.6 asks an LLM about it once per run, so a correctly-removed stop can return on the next run. D556 caught exactly that: Villa Leopolda removed at conf=high on one Cimiez run, kept on the next. This corpus makes the verdict deterministic.
_rule: An entry is keyed on the (name, scope) PAIR, never on the name alone — a venue outside Cimiez is perfectly in scope for a tour of the Riviera. `expect: "outside"` drops the stop. `expect: "verify"` is a suspicion on the record and must NEVER remove anything. Entries are appended automatically by scope_memory.record_out_of_scope() when PHASE 5.6 rejects at high confidence, which means the corpus can only make an existing removal consistent — it can never remove something the guard was not already willing to remove. Delete an entry if it is wrong; that is the correction path.
_consumed_by: scope_memory.known_out_of_scope(), called from _validate_stops_within_scope() in generate_tour_text.py before the LLM check. Regression suite: tests/test_d557_scope_memory.py
